Here is the Python code to classify the lines of the laboratory report:

```python
known_tests = {
    "718-7": "Haemoglobin",
    "789-8": "Red blood cells",
    "4544-3": "Haematocrit",
    "787-2": "MCV",
    "6690-2": "White blood cells",
    "777-3": "Platelets",
    "2498-4": "Iron",
    "2276-4": "Ferritin",
    "2345-7": "Glucose",
    "4548-4": "HbA1c",
    "2093-3": "Total cholesterol",
    "2085-9": "HDL cholesterol",
    "13457-7": "LDL cholesterol",
    "2571-8": "Triglycerides",
    "2160-0": "Creatinine",
    "3084-1": "Uric acid",
    "2951-2": "Sodium",
    "2823-3": "Potassium",
    "17861-6": "Calcium",
    "1742-6": "ALT",
    "1920-8": "AST",
    "2324-2": "GGT",
    "6768-6": "Alkaline phosphatase",
    "1975-2": "Total bilirubin",
    "1751-7": "Albumin",
    "3016-3": "TSH",
    "3024-7": "Free T4",
    "1988-5": "CRP",
    "62292-8": "Vitamin D (25-OH)",
    "2132-9": "Vitamin B12"
}

def classify_line(line):
    parts = line.split(":")
    number = parts[0].strip()
    test_name = parts[1].strip()
    if test_name in known_tests:
        return f"{number}|{known_tests[test_name]}"
    else:
        return f"{number}|NONE"

lines = [
    "1: Paziente: Maria Ferrari    Data di nascita: 04/09/1996",
    "2: Emoglobina                  13.1 g/dl     (12.0 - 16.0)",
    "3: Eritrociti                   6.5 10^6/uL  (4.0 – 5.5)",
    "4: Ematocrito                  46.2 %        (36.0-48.0)",
    "5: MCV                         81.4 fL       (80.0-100.0)",
    "6: Leucociti                   14.4 10^3/µL  (4.0 - 10.0)",
    "7: Piastrine (PLT)             98.4 10^3/µL  (150.0 – 450.0)",
    "8: Ferro                      187.0 µg/dL    (50.0 – 170.0)",
    "9: Ferritina                  120.5 ng/ml    (15.0-150.0)",
    "10: Glucosio                   109.9 mg/dL    (70.0-100.0)",
    "11: Emoglobina glicata           7.9 %        (< 5.7)",
    "12: Colesterolo totale         147.6 mg/dL    (< 200.0)",
    "13: Colesterolo HDL             77.0 mg/dL    (>40.0)",
    "14: Colesterolo LDL             85.7 mg/dL    (fino a 130.0)",
    "15: Trigliceridi               183.4 mg/dL    (<150.0)",
    "16: Creatinina                   0.5 mg/dL    (0.5 - 1.1)",
    "17: Acido. urico                 5.3 mg/dL    (3.0-7.0)",
    "18: S0dio                      187.9 mmol/l   (136.0 - 145.0)",
    "19: Potassio                     3.3 mmol/l   (3.5 - 5.1)",
    "20: Calcio                       9.6 mg/dL    (8.5 - 10.5)",
    "21: ALT                         50.4 U/L      (<40.0)",
    "22: AST (GOT)                   33.4 U/L      (<40.0)",
    "23: Gamma GT                    27.8 U/L      (< 50.0)",
    "24: Fosfatasl alcalina          97.3 U/L      (40.0-130.0)",
    "25: Bilirubina totale            1.7 mg/dl    (0.3 – 1.2)",
    "26: Albumina                     4.6 g/dL     (3.5 - 5.0)",
    "27: TSH                          0.9 miu/l    (0.4-4.0)",
    "28: FT4                          1.7 ng/dL    (0.9-1.7)",
    "29: Proteina C reattiva          4.5 mg/l     (<5.0)",
    "30: Vitami. D (25-OH)           36.9 ng/mL    (30.0-100.0)",
    "31: Vitamina B12               191.3 pg/ml    (200.0 – 900.0)",
    "32: Pag. 1/1"
]

for line in lines:
    print(classify_line(line))
```

This code defines a dictionary `known_tests` that maps LOINC codes to their corresponding English names. The `classify_line` function takes a line from the report as input, splits it into parts, and checks if the test name is in the `known_tests` dictionary. If it is, the function returns a line with the number and the corresponding LOINC code. If not, the function returns a line with the number and "NONE". The code then iterates over the lines of the report, prints the classified line for each one.
